blocks.content: Maya was in my doorway when I got home. Arms crossed, doing the face.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I ignored everyone equally. It's called fairness.
She didn't smile. I looked at my hands.

My sister is twenty-four and loves me in this very thorough, very attentive way that I'm genuinely grateful for. It also, sometimes, feels like being watched through glass. Warm. Safe. But the glass is always there.

blocks.speaker: Maya
blocks.content: You can't keep treating it like it's optional.
There's this specific frustration I get when someone says something I can't argue with. It has nowhere to go, so it just sits in my jaw.
That stung. Not because she was cruel. Because she was tired, and I made her tired, and those are connected.
I reached for Winston and picked at the loose thread near his arm.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I don't know. That's what made it funny.
I was smiling before I realized I was doing it. His face when he startled. The paint on his knuckle. The way he said technically like it was both a real answer and a joke at the same time.
Maya sat beside me on the bed.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: You were about to say it with your whole face.

blocks.speaker: Maya
blocks.content: I just don't want you to get hurt.
I laughed, but it came out flat.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: That's kind of unavoidable, isn't it.
Too much silence. I heard it as soon as it left my mouth. Maya looked away, eyes bright in a way I couldn't stand looking at.
We sat there with our hands linked, not saying the real thing. Outside the window the sky had gone lavender — last light sitting along the rooftops like it wasn't in any hurry.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I don't want every good thing filtered through fear.

blocks.speaker: Cassandra
blocks.content: I want a normal story, Maya.
My voice cracked on normal. I hate when that happens.
She put her head on my shoulder.
I closed my eyes and let myself believe it. I've gotten good at believing things for exactly as long as they're useful.
